features.name: example_comment_count
features.definition: How many counter-argument comments offer a specific real-world example as support?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments as a JSON list of comments by other users. Count comments that themselves offer at least one specific real-world example (a concrete actual case, event, person, study, statistic tied to a case, or personal experience) as support for their counter-argument. Hypothetical, generic or abstract illustrations do not count. Quotations of the OP or others count only if the commenter adopts them as their own example support. Ignore OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome resolution updates and reports of the outcome as evidence. Output a non-negative integer; 0 for a valid empty list; null if missing or malformed.

h0: example_comment_count has no association with the probability that the OP changed their view (delta).
h1: Higher example_comment_count is associated with a higher probability that the OP changed their view.
note: Operational assumption: "more counter-arguments" is read as the count of comments with specific real-world examples (not the share). OLS on binary delta is a linear probability model. Count depends on the number of available comments; no controls added. Comments may include outcome-related text, which the prompt excludes as evidence; comment order/timing unknown. Association only, not causal.
